task: capture10000 mouse target consumption source audit

findings.detail: ProcessInput reads mouse/UI state, finds CActorPickInfo with CActorPickNode::FindPickInfo, invokes ProcessMouseSnap, then skips actor/ground picking while quest/player-dead/exchange/item-store/mail/auction conditions hold. Otherwise ProcessActorPick then ProcessGroundPick then ProcessLockOnMouse. ProcessActorPick ignores actor picks for SUT_TO_GROUND; classType 3 suppresses selection when m_lastMonGid is active, classType 4 routes to object-click; otherwise selection is delegated to monster/PC handlers.

Input message case 0x4E explicitly clears skillUseType, skillId, and useLevel. Case 0x4F assigns skillUseType from val1 and skillId/range/level from the skill payload. ProceedAttack reads pending skill fields to issue player SendMsg 41 (target gid, skill id, attack range) plus SendMsg 90(level) when the type is 2 or 4, or SendMsg 10 for basic attack; it does not clear the pending skill fields. Another broad clear is at GameMode.cpp:10954-10956, outside the target-click path.

Left BTN_DOWN dispatches CMode::SendMsg(this,78,0,0,0) after pick processing. Right-click path also sends mode message 78 after message 19. The visible case 78 at line 4040 maps to effect/emotion mapping (case 78 -> v8=77) in a different switch; it is not evidence of target-click reset. A click-target flow can call ProceedAttack through other paths; no direct call was found by rg, so vtable/message dispatch or helper path remains to identify.

Actor source confirms burrow/hiding checks: effect message case 51 returns early for Burrow, Hiding, or cart effect; message case 126 skips the effect for special hiding, burrow, or hiding. Effect-state transition handling detects Burrow changes, deletes level effects, and on entering burrow emits object message 63 (with additional job-specific effect handling). These are rendering/effect behaviors, not proof of pick-node exclusion.

unresolved_questions: The exact CActorPickNode::FindPickInfo eligibility/exclusion logic and whether burrowed actors are omitted from pick results needs its implementation traced.
The actor-side receiver for player SendMsg message 41 should be checked to establish whether it clears or replaces an existing proceed target immediately.
No direct CGameMode::ProceedAttack call appears in the inspected source references; identify its indirect/vtable caller before asserting capture target-click consumption.
Setting a new capture skill appears to replace the pending skill-use fields in message 0x4F, but no adjacent clear of an already queued player proceed/attack target is established by these sources.
root_review_overrides: ProceedAttack itself does not clear pending fields, but the full world-input path does: Ref/GameMode.cpp14139-14145 dispatches mode78 AFTER actor/ground pick; Ref/GameMode2.cpp4887-4892 case0x4E clears skillUseType/id/useLevel. The bounded audit must not be read as pending intent surviving a world left-down/miss.

Root checked player message41 at Ref/Player.cpp400-421: when state!=6 and not burrow for10000, it replaces PT_SKILL/proceedTargetGid/skillId/attackRange. Message90 follows with level0.019E itself only assigns mode skill fields; it does not send player13 or clear an already queued chase.

Source primary monster-target click in Ref/GameMode.cpp6199 onward applies Shift/noShift and good-skill gates; do not assume generic NPC exclusion, PC or background behavior reproduces this flow. Full picking/consumption integration remains the next strong-agent task.
